/the-issue/.label: What happened
/the-issue/.text: APERS reported $25 million in Israel Bond positions on September 7, 2026. An ATRS manager account bought a $9.9 million Israel Bond on February 17, 2026, inside $50 million ATRS had transferred to it.

/the-issue/.label: What it means for members
/the-issue/.text: Members should be able to read the financial reasoning behind each decision: the repayment risk, the alternatives, access to the money and why it serves them.

/the-issue/.label: What it does not mean
/the-issue/.text: These records do not establish a loss to any member's benefit or require changes to individual retirement choices.

/evidence/.label: What the records show
/evidence/.text: What APERS held on September 7, 2026, and what ATRS's manager bought on February 17, 2026, each from a dated record you can open.

/evidence/.label: How to read the figures
/evidence/.text: The amounts come from different dates and cannot be added. ATRS's $9.9 million bond is part of its $50 million manager account, not on top of it.

/evidence/.label: What remains open
/evidence/.text: Aon gave ATRS substantive advice on choosing a manager and carrying out the investment. The open question is which decision-specific financial analysis trustees relied on, and where members can read it.

/evidence/apers/.label: What happened
/evidence/apers/.text: APERS custody reporting shows two Israel Bond positions totaling $25 million par, the bonds' face amount, on September 7, 2026.

/evidence/apers/.label: What it means for members
/evidence/apers/.text: How that amount is split among the systems APERS administers is unresolved, so it is not an individual member allocation.

/evidence/apers/.label: What remains open
/evidence/apers/.text: The reviewed records do not identify an independent consultant credit memo tied to either purchase. That describes what was produced, not proof that nothing else exists.

/evidence/atrs/.label: What happened
/evidence/atrs/.text: ATRS transferred $50 million to a Reams manager account on January 2, 2026. That account bought one $9.9 million Israel Bond on February 17, 2026.

/evidence/atrs/.label: How to read the figures
/evidence/atrs/.text: The bond is part of the $50 million, not in addition to it. In July the rest of the account was U.S. Treasuries and cash.

/evidence/atrs/.label: What remains open
/evidence/atrs/.text: Aon advised on choosing the manager but said its memo was not a recommendation to invest in Israel Bonds. The open question is the decision-specific financial case trustees relied on.

/educators/.label: What happened
/educators/.text: ATRS moved $50 million to an outside manager account on January 2, 2026. That account bought a $9.9 million Israel Bond on February 17, 2026.

/educators/.label: What it means for you
/educators/.text: You can ask where members can read the written financial case for that decision.

/educators/.label: What it does not mean
/educators/.text: These records do not establish a loss to your benefit or require changes to your individual retirement choices.

/public-employees/.label: What happened
/public-employees/.text: APERS custody reporting lists $25 million par in two Israel Bond positions as of September 7, 2026.

/public-employees/.label: What it means for you
/public-employees/.text: It is not an individual member allocation. You can ask where members can read the financial case for these positions.

/public-employees/.label: What it does not mean
/public-employees/.text: These records do not establish a loss to your benefit or require changes to your individual retirement choices.
